front: Name the three regions of a regurgitant jet used in quantitation.
back: Proximal flow convergence (PISA), vena contracta (narrowest segment), and the distal turbulent jet.

front: State the PISA formula for EROA.
back: EROA = (2π r² × V_aliasing) / V_peak regurg. Regurg volume = EROA × VTI_regurg.

front: What color-Doppler adjustment optimizes PISA hemisphere formation?
back: Shift the color baseline in the direction of the jet to reduce aliasing velocity to ~30–40 cm/s. This enlarges the PISA hemisphere and improves the accuracy of the radius measurement.

front: State the severe vena contracta widths for AR, MR, and TR.
back: Severe AR: VC > 0.6 cm. Severe MR: VC ≥ 0.7 cm. Severe TR: VC ≥ 0.7 cm.

front: How is the color-area (% of receiving chamber) method affected by an eccentric wall-hugging jet?
back: It UNDERESTIMATES severity — the Coanda effect makes wall-hugging jets appear smaller than they truly are. Use PISA, VC, or volumetric methods for accurate grading.

front: Downstream flow pattern in severe MR vs severe AR — where do you look?
back: Severe MR: SYSTOLIC pulmonary vein flow reversal. Severe AR: HOLODIASTOLIC flow reversal in the proximal descending / abdominal aorta.

front: Downstream flow pattern for severe TR? Severe PR?
back: Severe TR: systolic hepatic vein flow reversal. Severe PR: holodiastolic pulmonary artery flow reversal (below the pulmonic valve).

front: State the volumetric method for calculating MR volume.
back: RV_MR = SV_mitral − SV_LVOT, where SV_mitral = CSA_MV annulus × VTI_MV inflow and SV_LVOT = CSA_LVOT × VTI_LVOT. Only valid when the aortic valve is competent.

front: What is the acceptable color Nyquist range for JET-AREA analysis vs PISA?
back: Jet-area/color surveys: Nyquist ~50–70 cm/s. For PISA hemisphere: baseline-shifted Nyquist ~30–40 cm/s.

front: Why can a LOW peak velocity of an AR CW jet actually indicate severe (acute) AR?
back: Peak AR velocity reflects (aortic DBP − LVEDP). In acute severe AR, LVEDP rises rapidly while aortic DBP falls, so the gradient — and thus peak velocity — is small (rapid pressure equalization). Also produces steep deceleration / short PHT.
